title: Forms and validation
goal: Guide users through valid input and validate again on the server.
explanation: Native input types, required, min and max provide useful client-side constraints. Associate instructions and error messages with the relevant control.
Client validation improves usability but cannot enforce security. Requests can be sent without your page, so the server must independently validate type, length and allowed values.
Keep a failed submission available for correction. Explain what went wrong without exposing secrets or database internals. Never rely on a disabled button as an access-control check.
code:
<form>
  <label for="contact">Email</label>
  <input id="contact" name="email" type="email" required>
  <button type="submit">Request a reply</button>
</form>
exercise: Build a labelled email form. Describe the server validation it also needs.
hint: Client controls help the person; the server must distrust all incoming requests.

quiz.question: Where is security-critical input validation required?
options: On the server, even if the browser also validates
quiz.explanation: The server receives requests from any client, including clients that bypass your form.
